symptom: `create nanoflow M.X` over an existing microflow M.X (or a snippet over a page, an enumeration or association over an entity) reports success, `mxcli check --references` passes, and `mx check` then fails: [CE0122] "Duplicate document name 'M.X'." / [CE0065] "Duplicate name 'X' in module 'M'. Entities, associations and enumerations cannot share names."
cause: Every existence check was per kind: each handler, MDL-DUPDEF and CheckProjectConflicts asked only whether its own kind had the name. Mendix's rule is per NAME SPACE, and the name spaces are not 'all documents' — measured with mx check 11.14.0 over every pair of fourteen creatable kinds on TestApp copies, only {microflow, nanoflow, rule}, {page, snippet, layout} (CE0122) and {entity incl. view/external, association incl. cross-module, enumeration} (CE0065) clash; a microflow may share a name with a page, constant, enumeration, java action or workflow. Folders do not scope the name and the comparison is case-insensitive
file: mdl/executor/validate_name_clash.go (documentNameSpaces, refuseNameClash, CheckProjectNameClashes, checkScriptNameClash), wired in registry.go Dispatch, validate_duplicates.go, cmd/mxcli/cmd_exec.go pre-flight
fix: One table of shared name spaces; exec refuses in the dispatch before the handler writes, check reports MDL-DUPNAME within a script and CheckProjectConflicts / exec pre-flight report clashes with the project. A create whose own kind already has the name is skipped (it modifies or is refused as a duplicate), so `create or modify` inside a pre-existing clash still works. Layout added to stmtCreateKind so page/layout clashes are seen by check
insight: Do not guess a platform uniqueness rule from the issue text ('document names are unique per module') — it was wrong in both directions (entities are not documents but clash with enumerations; most document kinds never clash). Generate every pair into a TestApp copy and let mx check enumerate the rule; the same matrix, re-run through the fixed exec with --continue-on-error, is the end-to-end proof (only the clashing pairs fail, mx check 0 errors). Separately noticed: a same-kind create that differs only in case (`create nanoflow M.act_login` over nanoflow M.ACT_Login) is still created — the per-kind handlers compare exactly
